@TeleOp tells the Driver Station this OpMode should appear in the TeleOp list.

It has a 'name' parameter (what shows on screen) and a 'group' parameter (how OpModes are organized in the dropdown).

Autonomous OpModes use @Autonomous instead.

Your starter already has @TeleOp(name = "First OpMode", group = "Lessons").
The starter file already has the full OpMode skeleton: it extends OpMode, has @TeleOp, and has stubs for init() and loop().

init() is called once when you press the INIT button.

This is where you set up hardware: getting motors, configuring sensors.

For now, init() is empty and that's fine.

loop() runs repeatedly after you press START.

This is your main code.

For now, add telemetry.addData("Status", "Running"); inside loop() to confirm the OpMode is alive.
